turn_text: Right, I mean, you mentioned getting the economy back on track here after this COVID pandemic that we've gone through. There really is more that we need to do on addressing rural broadband. We talk about rural broadband, but really it's broadband access. There's some areas even around cities that don't have access. But one of the struggles I've had for the last few years is that so many of my Democrat colleagues didn't recognize the value of rural broadband and particularly things like telehealth. maybe one of the silver linings in the COVID-19 disease and the impact there is that it has been raised as a more important issue and I think part of that maybe that so many of the Democrats come from inner cities and so they just don't understand not having lots of choices around access to broadband and you know, whereas we all know Republicans and Democrats know how important it is that we can we can telework and it's just been highlighted even more with with COVID-19 the ability to telework to have our kids being able to get a good education and particularly If you have people working from home, have kids trying to do their school work, being able to keep up with the markets and what's going on there. So from a federal standpoint, we need to continue to help develop and provide more support and funding for our rural broadband development and rolling that out, both as a big infrastructure package, but also continuing to support that with the Farm Bill and appropriations bills. In general I think about rural broadband as it's the next electrification standard that we ought to do across the country to make sure everybody has that access.
